edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 12

source_text: Trahe me post te; curremus. Sponsa se trahi petit, quia nemo venit ad Verbum nisi Pater traxerit eum. Singularis petit: trahe me; pluralis promittit: curremus — quia ubi una anima trahitur, multae adulescentulae sequuntur. In odorem unguentorum tuorum: non in visu primo, sed in odore famae et praedicationis currunt, donec facie ad faciem videant.
pass_a_gloss: Draw me after you; we-will-run. Bride herself to-be-drawn asks, because no-one comes unto Word unless Father will-have-drawn him. Singular she-asks: draw me; plural she-promises: we-will-run...
pass_b_english: [[Draw me after you; we will run >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The Bride asks to be drawn, because [[no one comes to the Word unless the Father draws him >> Bible:John 6:44]]. She asks in the singular — draw me — and promises in the plural — we will run — because when one soul is drawn, many young women follow. [[Into the fragrance of your ointments >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]: they run not first by sight, but by the fragrance of fame and preaching, until they see face to face.
